Target audience: University students (STEM majors)

Section: section_1 — Introduction: Beyond 3D Intuition (0:00-0:45)

Lecture lines:
Visualize the sphere in dimensions beyond three. [Asset: SphereAnimation]
A hypersphere follows the equation sum x squared. [Asset: EquationAnimation]
Slices reveal circles in two dimensions. [Asset: SliceAnimation]
A 3D sphere slicing yields a 2D circle. [Asset: 3DSliceAnimation]
Expanding this logic leads to 4D geometry. [Asset: 4DGeometryAnimation]

Planned animations:
1. Intuitive Hook: Flash a 2D circle and 3D sphere side-by-side. Color: #FFFFFF.
2. Formalize: Display equation Σxᵢ² = R². Color: #FFD700.
3. Concept: Illustrate 3D sphere slicing into 2D circle on a plane. Color: #00FFFF.
4. Abstract: Extrapolate to 4D hypersphere moving through 3D space. Color: #FF69B4.
5. Application: Highlight the transformation from volume to boundary representation. Color: #32CD32.

Section: section_2 — Prerequisite Review: The Distance Formula (0:45-1:30)

Lecture lines:
Distance begins with the Pythagorean theorem. [Asset: PythagorasAnimation]
Euclidean distance extends to any dimension. [Asset: EuclideanAnimation]
Calculate the vector magnitude in N-space. [Asset: MagnitudeAnimation]

Planned animations:
1. Prerequisites: Display Pythagoras a² + b² = c². Color: #FFD700.
2. Expansion: Build Euclidean distance formula in 2D. Color: #00FFFF.
3. Formalization: Extend to n-dimensions d = √(x₁² +... + xₙ²). Color: #FF69B4.

Section: section_3 — The 'Empty' Core Paradox (1:30-2:45)

Lecture lines:
Most sphere volume migrates to the shell. [Asset: VolumeMigrationAnimation]
The center becomes hollow as dimensions grow. [Asset: HollowCoreAnimation]
Think of an orange with a giant peel. [Asset: OrangeAnalogyAnimation]
Almost all mass concentrates near the crust. [Asset: CrustMassAnimation]
Volume shifts away from the inner sphere. [Asset: ShiftAnimation]

Planned animations:
1. Intuitive Hook: Display a shrinking central core in a hypersphere. Color: #FF69B4.
2. Formalization: Display the volume shell integral expression. Color: #FFD700.
3. Visual Synthesis: Show the 'crust' of the hypersphere turning bright. Color: #32CD32.
4. Analogy: Use an orange cross-section animation. Color: #FF8C00.
5. Summary: Indicate the 99% volume concentration near the surface. Color: #FFFFFF.

Section: section_4 — The Corner Concentration Mystery (2:45-4:15)

Lecture lines:
Hyperspheres barely touch hypercube walls. [Asset: TouchAnimation]
Corners of the cube become increasingly vast. [Asset: CornersAnimation]
Points in high dimensions are very sparse. [Asset: SparsityAnimation]

Planned animations:
1. Intuitive Hook: Show a sphere inside a hypercube. Color: #FFFFFF.
2. Formalization: Indicate the distance from cube center to corner. Color: #FFD700.
3. Visual Synthesis: Highlight the empty corner spaces. Color: #00FFFF.

Section: section_5 — Real-World Application & Summary (4:15-5:00)

Lecture lines:
Data science uses distance for classification. [Asset: ClassificationAnimation]
Hyperspheres cluster similar user preferences efficiently. [Asset: ClusteringAnimation]
High-dimensional spaces defy our 3D intuition. [Asset: SummaryAnimation]

Planned animations:
1. Prerequisites: Show a scatter plot of high-dimensional points. Color: #FF69B4.
2. Formalization: Display the KNN search formula. Color: #FFD700.
3. Real-world: Animate a search engine clustering points. Color: #32CD32.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
